claim: The sensor port load (design case, maximum SPS30 current and 1.2 margin) fits FieldNode's 100 mW design allowance
law: P = V I x duty; SPS30 datasheet 65 mA maximum at 5 V, 60 s in 300 s; front end 1.5 mA held on (CAL [A3])

claim: In FieldNode's worst month the cell is charged with more energy than the node draws in a day
law: Energy balance; FND-CAL-001 worst-month storage 7.75 Wh/day (CAL [A7])
check: in 7.75 Wh/day, out 2.33 Wh/day

claim: A full 6 Ah LiFePO4 cell (80 % usable) runs the node 6.6 days without sun
law: Usable energy over average draw (97 mW) (CAL [A6])
check: claimed 6.6 days, estimate 6.6 days (ratio 1.00)

claim: The LiFePO4 cell is not charged below 0 degC; a cold spell is ridden through on the cell (4.6 days at -20 degC)
law: LiFePO4 charge temperature limit (cell maker's data, in FieldNode); capacity ratio 0.70 at -20 degC (FND-CAL-001)
check: Autonomy 4.6 days at -20 degC (CAL [A6]); the first partner's climate data must show no sub-zero spell longer than that

claim: A 20-byte uplink takes about 247 ms at SF9 on a 125 kHz channel
law: Semtech AN1200.13 time-on-air formula, 33 bytes with LoRaWAN overhead, 48 payload symbols (CAL [B2])
check: claimed 247 ms, estimate 247 ms (ratio 1.00)

claim: The worst-case uplink (SF12) stays under the 1 % duty cycle of an EU868 sub-band
law: ETSI EN 300 220 and LoRaWAN EU868 regional parameters; 1.81 s in each 300 s (CAL [B3])

claim: In US915 the 20-byte record fits the 400 ms dwell limit at SF9 (DR1 carries up to 53 bytes; DR0 at SF10 carries 11)
law: FCC 47 CFR 15.247 dwell time; LoRaWAN US915 regional parameters (CAL [B5])

claim: At 15 min on The Things Network the node keeps within 30 s of airtime a day up to SF9
law: The Things Network fair use policy, 30 s per device per day (CAL [B8])
check: 23.7 s/day <= 30 s/day

claim: The 16-bit ADC's step is not what limits the NO2 reading (the cell's noise is)
law: NO2-B43F sensitivity -200 to -650 nA/ppm (Alphasense datasheet); 0.8 mV/nA front end; ADS1115 62.5 uV step
check: 0.16 to 0.52 mV/ppb, so one ADC step is 0.12 to 0.39 ppb, 20 to 60 times below the 7.5 ppb noise per sample (CAL [C1])

claim: Noise term of the hourly NO2 budget: per-sample noise taken from the sensor datasheet
law: NO2-B43F datasheet noise 15 ppb at 2 sigma; averaging 120 samples an hour divides it by the square root of 120
check: Was 5 ppb (1 sigma) assumed over 120 samples (Fails, fix proposed); now 7.5 ppb over the 12 independent records of an hour (the 10 samples of a record fall within the cell's response time), 2.17 ppb hourly, total 5.45 ppb, MAE 4.3 ppb (CAL [C2], [C3])

claim: After field calibration the hourly NO2 mean absolute error is about 4.3 ppb, within 5 ppb
law: Field-calibrated residual 3.5 ppb MAE (Zimmerman et al., 2018, a model that also drew on other gas sensors on the node, so optimistic for WE, AE, T and RH alone); drift, street transfer bias and a 5 % slope error assumed (CAL C)
check: Budget 5.45 ppb (1 sigma), MAE 4.3 ppb; only collocation at TRL 4 can show it (PR-002 at risk)

claim: An annual NO2 mean cannot be resolved to 2 ug/m3, so AirStreet makes no claim at the WHO guideline
law: Systematic terms do not average out over a year (CAL [C4])

claim: 1 ppb of NO2 is 1.88 ug/m3 at 25 degC, and 1.91 ug/m3 at the 20 degC the EU directive uses for limit values
law: Ideal gas molar volume 24.465 L/mol at 25 degC and 24.055 L/mol at 20 degC; NO2 46.006 g/mol; Directive 2008/50/EC refers gas volumes to 293 K (CAL [C1], [C5])
check: claimed 1.913 ug/m3 per ppb at 20 degC, estimate 1.91 ug/m3 per ppb at 20 degC (ratio 1.00)

claim: The NO2 cell's ozone filter lasts until the cell is replaced
law: NO2-B43F datasheet: ozone filter capacity more than 500 ppm h at 0.5 ppm O3; operating life more than 24 months (to 50 % signal)
check: At 40 to 60 ppb mean ozone the filter is used up in 17 to 11 months, before the 24-month replacement assumed before (Fails, fix proposed); now the cell is replaced every 12 months at the pod exchange, or at 18 or 24 months where the site's ozone record keeps the dose under 500 ppm h (CAL [C7])

claim: Every reading taken outside the sensors' rated temperature and humidity ranges is marked as such in the data
law: NO2-B43F rated -30 to 40 degC and 15 to 85 % RH continuous; SPS30 recommended 10 to 40 degC and 20 to 80 % RH (datasheets)
check: Rated-range flags in every record: shield air above 35 degC (a 5 K pod allowance, to measure at TRL 4), RH above 80 % or 85 % and below 20 % or 15 %, below 10 degC for PM; flagged hours are published with the flag (CAL [H5])

claim: The NO2 cell and the particle sensor measure validly across the whole climate the node is built for (-10 to 50 degC, 10 to 100 % RH)
law: NO2-B43F rated -30 to 40 degC and 15 to 85 % RH continuous; SPS30 recommended 10 to 40 degC and 20 to 80 % RH (datasheets)
check: Above 40 degC and 85 % RH the cell runs outside its rating; the flags (S15) mark those hours but do not make them valid. Fixes that change the user-facing scope (a wider-range cell, or a narrower PR-012) go to Amish (AST-DEC-001, open decision 3)

claim: After humidity correction the hourly PM2.5 error stays within 5 ug/m3 or 30 % up to 80 % RH
law: Laser scattering counts particles; kappa-Koehler water uptake 1 + kappa aw / (1 - aw), kappa 0.3 +/- 0.1 assumed (CAL E)
check: Within the bound to 80 % RH, outside it at 85 % RH and above at 25 and 50 ug/m3 (CAL [E2]); the comparison is at 1 sigma (about 68 % of hours), the base error and kappa are assumed and the RH is the shield's, not the pod's, so collocation at TRL 4 confirms it

claim: The passive eight-plate shield keeps the radiation error of the air temperature under 1 K at 1 m/s wind in full sun
law: Plate energy balance and probe convection (Zukauskas), inner air at 10 to 30 % of the wind (assumed) (CAL D)

claim: A 0.87 K warm error reads about 4.1 % RH low at 85 % RH and 30 degC
law: Magnus saturation vapour pressure (Sonntag constants) (CAL [D3])
check: claimed 4.1 % RH, estimate 4.13 % RH (ratio 0.99)

claim: A 35 m/s gust puts about 125 N on the node
law: F = 0.5 rho v^2 Cd A, Cd 1.2 on the 0.139 m2 model silhouette; 35 m/s is a screening speed, 206 N at 45 m/s for windier codes (CAL [G1])
check: claimed 125 N, estimate 125 N (ratio 1.00)

claim: Two bands hold the node against slipping down the pole
law: Belt friction F = mu T theta per band, 1,000 N preload and mu 0.3 assumed; load is weight and wind on the tilted panel (CAL [G2])

claim: The 40 x 4 mm rail at the lower clamp stays below the yield of 6063 aluminium with a factor of 1.5, in bending and twist together
law: Bending M / Z and flat-bar torsion T / (0.31 b t^2), von Mises; 6063-T5 minimum yield about 110 MPa (CAL [G6], [G8])
check: 33.2 MPa <= 73 MPa

claim: The cross arm carries the pod and the shield far below yield (with a factor of 1.5)
law: Combined bending of a 30 x 30 x 3 angle (CAL [G3])
check: 4.4 MPa <= 100 MPa

claim: The 12.7 x 0.6 mm stainless band carries its 1,000 N preload below yield (with a factor of 1.5)
law: Tension stress T / (w t); 304 stainless, minimum yield 205 MPa annealed (ASTM A240); worm-drive bands are cold rolled and stronger, but slotted
check: Gross section 131 MPa against 137 MPa; at the worm slots, with about 35 % of the section cut away, about 200 MPa; to confirm with the band maker's rated tension (AST-DEC-001, to confirm item 1)

claim: The band thickness used for the mass is the one in the model
law: One source of dimensions: the calculation reads PARAMS (STANDARDS section 24)
check: The model drew a 0.8 mm band while the mass used 0.6 mm (Fails, fix proposed); now 0.6 mm in the model and read from it (CAL [F4])

claim: Printed ASA saddles keep the band preload over years in sun
law: ASA is UV stable outdoors; printed thermoplastics creep under sustained load, faster when warm (heat deflection of ASA about 95 degC at 0.45 MPa)
check: Contact stress on the V faces is low (a few MPa), but creep at up to about 60 degC surface temperature can relax the preload; a re-torque at the first pod exchange and a check at TRL 4

claim: The pod's two hanging screws hold in their heat-set inserts with a wide margin
law: Worst pull-out per screw from weight and wind prying about the 40 mm bearing edge, shared by the two screws in line (CAL [G7]), against an M5 insert in printed ASA
check: About 11 N per screw against an assumed 200 N for the insert, which is not yet from maker data and falls when the ASA is warm; pull test at 23 and 60 degC at TRL 4 (AST-DEC-001, to confirm item 8)

claim: Traffic NO2 varies several fold within city blocks, so street-level nodes see what a city station misses
law: Apte et al. (2017), Oakland: NO2 varied 5 to 8 times within single blocks; WHO ambient air quality fact sheet
check: Cited as the problem, not as a health claim; AirStreet gives indicative levels, not health advice

claim: Inlets 3.0 m above the sidewalk sample the street air people breathe closely enough to rank streets
law: EU Directive 2008/50/EC Annex III: inlets 1.5 to 4 m above ground; Defra diffusion tube guidance: 2 to 4 m, higher tubes may read low
check: Inside the regulated range; a small vertical gradient is part of the transfer bias term (CAL C)

claim: A 60 s particle run leaves at least 30 s of valid readings in clean air
law: SPS30 datasheet: up to 30 s to the first reading at low counts (CAL [A9])

claim: The node with FieldNode's sun shield stays within 4.0 kg on the pole
law: Part volumes from the model and densities (CAL [F5])

claim: Stainless insect mesh under the pod keeps insects and spiders out of the sensors
law: Insect screens stop insects larger than the aperture; spiders and wasps nest in sheltered openings
check: Mesh aperture to be chosen for the smallest local insects; nesting is checked at each pod exchange (TRL 4)

claim: Twelve 10 s NO2 readings and twelve 60 s PM runs an hour represent the hourly mean
law: Sampling a fluctuating signal: the error of the hourly mean falls with the number of independent samples; the cell's response (T90 under 80 s) smooths the NO2 signal
check: Street NO2 changes over seconds near traffic; the sampling error is not in the budget and is measured in the TRL 4 collocation against the reference's continuous record

claim: The printed and bolted parts survive years of wind vibration and occasional ice
law: Fatigue under vortex shedding and gusts; ice load on the shield and panel
check: Stresses are low (S21, S22), but no fatigue or ice case is calculated; nyloc nuts and inserts resist loosening; checked at TRL 4 and by inspection at each pod exchange

claim: FieldNode's core survives 50 degC ambient with its sun shield fitted above 45 degC
law: FieldNode is rated to 45 degC ambient and runs 58.7 to 73.3 degC inside at 45 degC (FND-CAL-001); the sun shield is FieldNode's fix
check: To confirm in FieldNode's calculation note; AirStreet relies on it at hot sites

claim: Option B: a 30 W panel charges more than the heated, pumped node uses in a winter day
law: Energy balance with estimated loads (pump 1 W at 20 %, heater 2 W for 30 % of hours, fan 0.25 W, sensors 0.1 W)
check: in 45 Wh/day, out 27.6 Wh/day

claim: Option B: warming the 1 L/min sample by 5 K takes far less than the 2 W heater gives
law: P = m_dot cp dT; most of the heater power is lost through the sleeve

claim: Option B: warming the sample 5 K brings 90 % RH below the SPS30's 80 % recommended limit
law: Magnus saturation vapour pressure at 20 and 25 degC

claim: Option B: the heated inlet does not change the particles it measures
law: Semi-volatile ammonium nitrate evaporates when an inlet is heated (known loss in heated-inlet PM monitors)
check: A few kelvin of warming loses part of the nitrate fraction; to quantify by collocation if B were chosen

claim: Option C: a Palmes tube collects about 1.5 ug of NO2 in 28 days at 30 ug/m3
law: Fick's first law, uptake D A / L with D(NO2) 0.154 cm2/s, 11 mm bore, 71 mm long
check: claimed 1.5 ug, estimate 1.5 ug (ratio 1.00)

claim: Option C: triplicate tubes give monthly NO2 means within about 25 %
law: Defra NO2 diffusion tube practical guidance: indicative technique, uncertainty about 25 %; bias adjusted by collocation with a chemiluminescence analyser
check: Monthly means only; no hourly or daily data

claim: Option C: four alkaline D cells run the particle logger for a month between tube changes
law: Energy balance; alkaline D capacity about 12 Ah at low drain (estimate)
check: in 50.4 Wh, out 14.6 Wh
